name: broker-beachhead
concept: Post-exploitation pivot/infra kit for the lab: it parses the compromised host's local broker state (listeners, peers, stored service descriptors), then stands up a SOCKS-over-TCP or HTTP CONNECT tunnel through the beachhead to rediscover the internal lab network and route traffic into it. Bundles a mini-C2 check-in loop (HTTP beacon with lab-safe persistence via scheduled task/cron-style re-run) plus an explicit kill-switch and full cleanup that tears down tunnels, removes beacon artifacts, and restores original state.
attack_vectors: broker-state parsing to auto-discover internal lab subnets from the beachhead host
SOCKS-over-TCP/HTTP CONNECT pivot tunnel routing internal lab traffic through the compromised host
mini-C2 check-in loop with lab-safe persistence (scheduled re-run) and heartbeat
kill-switch + full cleanup reversing all persistence and tearing down tunnels to leave no residue
novelty_angle: Most pivot kits focus on raw port-forwarding; this derives the internal network map from the compromised host's own broker state and makes the C2 loop + kill-switch first-class, self-contained deliverables with reversible cleanup — a post-exploitation infra kit rather than a single tunnel.
dependencies: windows-schtasks or cron/systemd-timer for beacon re-run
asyncio or threading for concurrent tunnel/beacon
optional paramiko only if SSH pivoting needed
scope_gate: Single scope-gate module (allowlist = loopback + private ranges + user-supplied lab CIDR) validates every destination the tunnel routes to and every target the beacon checks in from; WARN banner on first run; hard-refuses any target outside the allowlist including broker-derived subnets not whitelisted.
